hints.title: Zero Fill Frequency Sequence Generation
hints.text: Count transactions per user visit, and use a recursive CTE to produce continuous transaction counts from 0 up to max transactions.

hints.title: Left Join Visits with Transactions
hints.text: Left join Visits with Transactions on user_id and visit_date to determine count of transactions completed on each visit.

hints.title: Recursive Sequence Join Blueprint
hints.text: with recursive Numbers as (select 0 as n union all select n + 1 from Numbers where n < (select max(cnt) from VisitTxns)) join Numbers with VisitTxns counts.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH RECURSIVE VisitTxns AS (
    SELECT v.user_id, v.visit_date, COUNT(t.transaction_date) AS txn_count
    FROM Visits v
    LEFT JOIN Transactions t ON v.user_id = t.user_id AND v.visit_date = t.transaction_date
    GROUP BY v.user_id, v.visit_date
),
MaxVal AS (
    SELECT IFNULL(MAX(txn_count), 0) AS max_n FROM VisitTxns
),
Numbers AS (
    SELECT 0 AS n
    UNION ALL
    SELECT n + 1 FROM Numbers, MaxVal WHERE n < max_n
)
SELECT num.n AS transactions_count, COUNT(vt.user_id) AS visits_count
FROM Numbers num
LEFT JOIN VisitTxns vt ON num.n = vt.txn_count
GROUP BY num.n
ORDER BY num.n;
```

complexity.notes: Recursive CTE generates integer range [0..M] followed by grouping on visit transaction counts.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Grouping directly on visits omits intermediate transaction count frequencies with zero occurrences.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Recursive generator guarantees gap-free integer continuum without hardcoding table literals.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recursive CTE sequence generation and left join with visit transactions.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def draw_chart(visits: pd.DataFrame, transactions: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    txns = transactions.groupby(['user_id', 'transaction_date']).size().reset_index(name='txn_count')
    merged = visits.merge(txns, left_on=['user_id', 'visit_date'], right_on=['user_id', 'transaction_date'], how='left')
    merged['txn_count'] = merged['txn_count'].fillna(0).astype(int)
    counts = merged.groupby('txn_count').size().to_dict()
    max_txn = merged['txn_count'].max() if not merged.empty else 0
    res = []
    for n in range(max_txn + 1):
        res.append({'transactions_count': n, 'visits_count': counts.get(n, 0)})
    return pd.DataFrame(res)
solutions.approach: Pandas Full Integer Range Generator and Count Mapping
